text:
sara: heads-up: noticed several tenants showing small but consistent positive diffs in invoice_preview (~0.5-1%) that align with streaming-heavy workloads (websocket streaming + function calls).
devin: can you paste an example trace?
sara: sure, pulled from debug capture: ```
{"tenant":"ACME","request_id":"r-42","events":[{"type":"stream_chunk","ts":1720001000,"tokens":8,"interim":true},{"type":"stream_chunk","ts":1720001002,"tokens":5,"interim":true},{"type":"finalize","ts":1720001003,"tokens":13,"interim":false}],"route":"stream-primary","model":"gptx-lite"}
```
sara: invoice_preview currently counts stream_chunk events as billable units and then also counts finalize->tokens, so the same tokens are appearing twice in preview aggregate.
eli: oy. Our ingestion proto lets streaming frames be emitted to metering with event_kind=TOKEN_EMIT and finalize events with TOKEN_SUMMARY. The ledger aggregation sums both.
devin: why did we change that? I thought streaming frames were only for real-time metrics, not billing.
eli: historical reason: early streaming impl surfaced chunks directly and billing later relied on stream events for low-latency metering. finalize was later added for atomicity and replay safety. We never deduped when both are present.
ops-bot: ALERT: invoice_preview_streaming_dup detected  22 tenants affected, median extra tokens = 18/tenant (alert id ef12).
billing-bot: sample tenant ACME preview shows +18 tokens vs canonical invoice for last hour.
sara: quick mitigation: add a simple rule in the preview pipeline to prefer finalize (TOKEN_SUMMARY) over TOKEN_EMIT if both share request_id; drop interim TOKEN_EMIT from billing aggregate. low-risk and reversible.
devin: sounds reasonable. Can we instead flag interim events with billable=false at source for streaming to avoid transport overhead?
eli: that requires multi-service change (runtime + proxy + ingest) and is not safe to push quickly. pipeline-side coalescing is faster.
console-ui: for visibility, we should add a new telemetry metric: "streaming_interim_bill_events_count" and a dashboard card for "finalize_vs_stream_ratio" per model/route.
sara: agreed. i'll add the pipeline rule as a feature-flagged job and a 5% canary. deploy plan: patch preview-aggregator, enable flag for 5% traffic, monitor billing-bot diffs + finalize_vs_stream_ratio for 30m, then 100% if good.
devin: add unit test to ensure if finalize arrives after stream chunks we ignore prior chunks, and if finalize missing we still accept chunks (safe fallback).
eli: also add sampling to store raw stream_chunk traces for 0.1% tenants to audit dedupe correctness during rollout.
sara: risk: long-tail clients that never send finalize (edge mobile disconnect) would previously be billable via chunks; new rule would drop them unless we keep fallback. so we must preserve behavior: if no finalize within 10s, count the last seen chunked sum.
devin: ok implement windowed fallback: if finalize not observed within 10s of first chunk, mark last-chunk-sum as final and emit TOKEN_SUMMARY then. tests + telemetry required.
sara: timeline: implement in preview pipeline + tests (45m), deploy canary (5% for 30m), watch alert + diffs, ramp to 100% over 1hr. rollback: flip feature flag off or revert aggregator job.
eli: i'll prepare the short runbook entries: query to find tenants with increases after change, how to trigger backfill for 10 tenants, and manual reconcile steps.
ops-bot: NOTE: automated backfill job available (backfill-metering v2) but needs opt-in for affected tenants.
billing-bot: reminder: coordinate with finance if we run backfills as credits; they prefer windowed reconciliation vs issuing ad-hoc adjustments.
sara: will loop in finance after canary. thanks all.
devin: thanks. ping me if you need proxy/runtime changes later.
eli: filing a follow-up doc in #docs-metering with event schema and aggregator pseudocode.
sara: ending thread; will post deploy start time in 20m.
